kurz: Milk proteins wrap around beaten-in air bubbles and hold them, best at 55–65 °C (as a guide).
bild_im_kopf: Like soap bubbles with a protein skin: the skin holds as long as it does not overheat.
was_passiert: Frothing beats air into the [[milch|milk]]. The milk proteins gather around the bubbles and form a stable skin. If the milk gets hotter than about 70 °C, the [[eiweiss-denaturierung|proteins change]] too much: the foam collapses and the milk tastes cooked.
warum_wichtig: Cold, fresh milk froths best. Whole milk gives creamier foam, skimmed milk more volume but drier.
faustregeln: For firm foam: cold, fresh milk, heated to no more than about 65 °C.
Foam collapses at once? The milk was too hot or had been heated before.
schritte: Pour cold milk into a cold jug, no more than a third full.
First draw in air until the volume has grown by about a third.
Then dip deeper and let the milk swirl until the jug is too hot to hold.
Tap and swirl briefly so large bubbles disappear.
